findings.evidence: Limits.lean declares only piFan/piFanIsLimit/equalizerFork/equalizerForkIsLimit and the HasProducts/HasEqualizers instances (grep of TauCeti/Topology/Category/TopCommRingCat/Limits.lean); none occurs in CompleteSeparated.lean's proof term or statements — the pi theorem writes its apex out as `TopCommRingCat.of (∀ b, f b)`, not `(piFan f).pt`. FullSubcategory reachability: `grep -l '^public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory' mathlib/Mathlib` hits Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ConcreteCategory/Basic.lean.
findings.fix: Replace with `public import Mathlib.Topology.Category.TopCommRingCat`. `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` remains in scope through it (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ConcreteCategory/Basic.lean imports Mathlib.CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory, and Mathlib.Topology.Category.TopCommRingCat depends on ConcreteCategory via Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Ring.Basic).
findings.issue: `public import TauCeti.Topology.Category.TopCommRingCat.Limits` supplies no declaration the file uses; `piFan`, `piFanIsLimit`, `equalizerFork`, `HasProducts`, `HasEqualizers` appear only in docstrings. It is present solely as an indirect path to Mathlib's `TopCommRingCat`, and so forces every downstream consumer of the predicate/subcategory to pull the limits construction and its global `HasProduct`/`HasLimit (parallelPair)` instances.

summary: Placement is correct — the file joins the existing TopCommRingCat/ subdirectory and the predicate is genuinely generic. One import is wrong: TauCeti...TopCommRingCat.Limits is used for nothing in the file body and only serves as an indirect route to Mathlib's TopCommRingCat.
